goalsQuestion: What upload and download traffic, file sizes, metadata latency and download-start targets should I use?
constraintsQuestion: What do upload completion, concurrent versions, retention, cleanup and revoked access guarantee?
requirementsAnswer: I will estimate upload and download traffic from the agreed daily volumes and ten-times peak factor, use a 10 MB average and 1 GB maximum file size, target p95 metadata latency below 200 milliseconds and download start below 1 second, and preserve the 7-day old-version and 24-hour abandoned-upload defaults.
coreExplanation: The upload API authorizes the owner and issues a stable upload ID with numbered resumable parts and checksums; only after complete durable bytes pass verification does a transaction publish the file metadata, and repeating completion returns the original published result.

File metadata stores owner, read grants, current version and the immutable byte-object ID; replacement includes the base version and a conditional update rejects a stale device with a conflict, keeping older completed versions for 7 days rather than silently overwriting them.
validationExplanation: For downloads the API checks ownership or an active read grant and issues a ticket expiring within 60 seconds, so revocation stops new tickets and existing ones expire within the bound; a cleanup worker uses metadata references and last-progress time to reclaim abandoned parts after 24 hours without deleting an active upload.

For a popular large file I separate metadata requests from bulk byte transfer and measure throughput, download-start latency, interrupted-part retries, storage and egress cost; I would load-test concurrent 1 GB uploads and a failure after byte completion but before metadata publication, then recover or safely collect the unreferenced object.
rubricEvidence: I will estimate upload and download traffic
weakAnswer: I mark an upload complete as soon as its metadata exists, restart the entire 1 GB transfer after any interruption, let a stale device overwrite the current version, and allow anyone who guesses the file ID to download it forever.
reviewFocus: Publishing metadata before complete durable bytes exposes broken downloads.
Restarting all bytes does not meet resumable upload behavior and stale replacement loses another device's work.
A file identifier is not authorization and perpetual access cannot satisfy bounded revocation.
